title: Are circuits clustered in low-dimensional space?

cues.en: In this video, I am going to show you an investigation into identifying circuits based on clustering in a lower dimensional space.
cues.zh: 這支影片，會展示一項研究，根據低維空間中的分群，辨識迴路。

cues.en: Now, it sounds like it should be a very sensible and successful analysis approach to take, but I can already tell you that is not going to work.
cues.zh: 聽起來應該是合理、能成功的分析方法，但可以先說，它不會成功。

cues.en: Well, the analysis will work, but they will not reveal meaningful circuits or clusters in the way that we might want.
cues.zh: 分析本身會運作，但不會以我們想要的方式，揭示有意義的迴路或群集。

cues.en: But that's actually fantastic, because if you want to advance research, you need to know what works.
cues.zh: 不過其實很好，因為要推進研究，需要知道什麼有效，

cues.en: And you also need to know what is unlikely to work.
cues.zh: 也需要知道什麼不太可能有效。

cues.en: And also, the methods that I will implement in this code demo are great reminders of some analysis
cues.zh: 另外，這份程式示範實作的方法，也能很好地複習一些分析

cues.en: techniques, including t-SNE, DBscan, and K-means clustering.
cues.zh: 技巧，包括 t-SNE、DBSCAN，以及 K-means 分群。

cues.en: Essentially, what I'm going to do here is statistically Identify MLP expansion neurons from one transformer
cues.zh: 基本上，要從一個 Transformer 區塊，透過統計找出 MLP 擴張

cues.en: block that have significantly different activation magnitudes for either him or her, so the pronouns
cues.zh: 神經元，對 him 或 her 的活化大小有顯著差異，

cues.en: him or her using the him and her sentences that we've used a few times before in this course.
cues.zh: 也就是用課程中用過幾次的 him、her 句子，研究這兩個代名詞。

cues.en: Then we will see if we can use clustering to group these neurons into small circuits that are basically behaving in very similar ways.
cues.zh: 接著看看，能否用分群，將神經元組成行為基本上非常相似的小迴路。

cues.en: So yeah, it's a quite a sensible thing to do, but it turns out that it's not going to yield a reproducible
cues.zh: 這是相當合理的做法，但結果不會得到可重現的

cues.en: set of small clusters, at least not in this model that I will use here and not in the data set that I have used here.
cues.zh: 小群集，至少這裡使用的模型與資料集如此。

cues.en: Perhaps the analysis approach could be useful, could be more fruitful for other models.
cues.zh: 這個分析方式，也許對其他模型有用、更有成果，

cues.en: Maybe we would just need a much larger data set.
cues.zh: 也許只需要大得多的資料集。

cues.en: So I don't want to dismiss the approach that I will show you here completely out of hand.
cues.zh: 所以不想完全、不加考慮地否定這個方法。

cues.en: But by the end of this video, I think you will agree that this approach was worth learning about, but doesn't really give a nice set of results.
cues.zh: 但影片結束時，我想你會同意，方法值得學習，卻沒有得到很好的結果。

cues.zh: 同樣，如果資料真的形成群集，就預期對角線出現像這樣的區塊。

cues.en: This one actually looks really nice.
cues.zh: 這一個其實很好看。

cues.en: You would want to see blocks on the diagonal such that within the block the cosine similarity is really
cues.zh: 希望看到對角線上的區塊，區塊內餘弦相似度非常

cues.en: high, and off of that block the cosine similarities are very low, close to zero, maybe a little bit
cues.zh: 高，區塊外則很低、接近零，也許稍微

cues.en: negative if there's some negative lateral interactions amongst the different clusters.
cues.zh: 為負，如果不同群集之間有負向側向交互作用。

cues.en: But that's not really the case here.
cues.zh: 但這裡不太是如此，

cues.en: So also when I look at this I do not see evidence of clustering okay.
cues.zh: 看這個結果，也看不到分群證據。

cues.en: So again you know we are really not statistically justified to do a k means analysis.
cues.zh: 同樣，統計上沒有充分理由做 K-means，

cues.en: But this is a really nice opportunity for you to see the code again for k means clustering just to get some more familiarity with it.
cues.zh: 但這是再次查看 K-means 分群程式、增加熟悉度的好機會。

cues.en: And because, you know, this is all just gobbledygook.
cues.zh: 反正這些都只是亂七八糟，

cues.en: Anyway, why don't we change the number of clusters to 13?
cues.zh: 那為什麼不把群數改成 13？

cues.en: Because why not?
cues.zh: 為什麼不呢？

cues.en: That's a lucky number I think.
cues.zh: 我想那是幸運數字。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: So here's the k means function.
cues.zh: 這是 K-means 函式，

cues.en: I specify 13 clusters and then I fit the t-SNE results.
cues.zh: 指定 13 群，再擬合 t-SNE 結果，

cues.en: And then I generate the plot.
cues.zh: 接著產生圖形。

cues.en: Here I'm plotting not only all the individual data points, but also the central the centroid of each data point.
cues.zh: 不只畫所有個別資料點，也畫出每個資料點的中心、質心。

cues.en: So this is the centroid of this cluster.
cues.zh: 這是這個群集的質心，

cues.en: This is the centroid of this cluster and so on.
cues.zh: 這是另一群的質心，依此類推。

cues.en: And here is again cosine similarities sorted.
cues.zh: 這裡再次是排序後的餘弦相似度，

cues.en: So all the neurons sorted according to their group identity over here.
cues.zh: 所有神經元，依照這裡的群組身分排序。

cues.en: Now even if you think that these are like real clusters which I hope you don't think when you run the
cues.zh: 即使你覺得它們是真實群集，希望你不會這樣想，重新執行

cues.en: code again you will get very different results just because of the random initialization involved in K-means clustering.
cues.zh: 程式，也會因為 K-means 的隨機初始化，而得到很不同的結果。

cues.en: A quote that I like a lot, which I find very often relevant, especially when I ran a neuroscience
cues.zh: 有一句話我很喜歡，經常覺得很貼切，尤其以前主持神經科學

cues.en: research lab and had a lot of students and postdocs in my lab doing research.
cues.zh: 研究室，有很多學生與博士後進行研究時，

cues.en: Is this quote here from Alexander Graham Bell?
cues.zh: 就是 Alexander Graham Bell 的這句話。

cues.en: There are no unsuccessful experiments.
cues.zh: 沒有不成功的實驗，

cues.en: Every experiment contains a lesson.
cues.zh: 每個實驗都包含一個教訓。

cues.en: So Bell, of course, was the guy who invented the telephone.
cues.zh: Bell 當然就是發明電話的人，

cues.en: Not a bad legacy to leave behind.
cues.zh: 留下這樣的成就，很不錯。

cues.en: Uh, and what this quote means is that every experiment that you do, every data analysis you run, there's always something to learn.
cues.zh: 這句話的意思，是每個實驗、每項資料分析，永遠都有東西可學，

cues.en: Even if you do not get the results that you are hoping for.
cues.zh: 即使結果不是期待的，

cues.en: There's always something useful to be learned, even from unexpected or disappointing results.
cues.zh: 即使意外或令人失望，仍然能學到有用的東西。

cues.en: Now, to be honest, this is also something that annoys me very much about our scientific publishing culture.
cues.zh: 老實說，這也是科學發表文化中，非常令我煩惱的事。

cues.en: You know, we are incentivized to publish positive results and especially results that are surprising or unexpected.
cues.zh: 我們被鼓勵發表正向結果，尤其令人驚訝、出乎意料的結果。

cues.en: But there is so much to learn about how complex systems work and how they don't work.
cues.zh: 但關於複雜系統如何運作、如何不運作，其實有太多可以學，

cues.en: By studying the analyses that seem like they should be insightful but end up not working out anyway.
cues.zh: 透過研究那些看似應該有啟發，最後卻不成功的分析。

cues.en: So that's that.
cues.zh: 就是這樣。

cues.en: I don't mean to be so dismissive or to dismiss this method.
cues.zh: 不想如此輕率否定，也不想否定這個方法。

cues.en: It is very possible that this kind of approach would be much more successful.
cues.zh: 這類做法很可能，在某些情況成功得多，

cues.en: Maybe for larger models, maybe for different kinds of target tokens, slightly different analyses, or maybe in different parts of the model.
cues.zh: 也許更大模型、其他目標 token、稍微不同的分析，或模型其他部分。

cues.en: For example, you have seen that this exact same analysis approach was actually quite useful earlier
cues.zh: 例如，課程前面，研究不同嵌入矩陣的 token 嵌入時，

cues.en: in the course when we were studying token embeddings with different embeddings matrices.
cues.zh: 就看過完全相同的分析方式，其實相當有用。
